22 Token_t *create_token(int line, int col, int type, const char *text)
23  {
24  Token_t *tmp_token = NULL;
25 
26  // DQ (11/5/2016): Can't use C++ "delete" in token.c file from OFP jar file since it is compiled using a C compiler (so use malloc here).
27  // DQ (11/5/2016): Updated the token.c file in the OFP jar file to fix this bug and make the new (here) consistant with the delete (there).
28  // DQ (11/4/2016): Since in the OFP this is deleted using free (token.c in the build tree), we want
29  // to allocate it using the associated C style malloc (bug caught using address sanitizer).
30  // DQ (9/11/2011): We want to use the C++ new and delete memory allocation
31  // and not mix C's malloc/free with C++'s new/delete mechanisms.
32  // tmp_token = (Token_t*) malloc(sizeof(Token_t));
33  // tmp_token = new Token_t();
34  tmp_token = (Token_t*) malloc(sizeof(Token_t));
35  ROSE_ASSERT(tmp_token != NULL);
36  tmp_token->line = line;
37  tmp_token->col = col;
38  tmp_token->type = type;
39  /* Make a copy of our own to make sure it isn't freed on us. */
40  if (text != NULL)
41  tmp_token->text = strdup(text);
42  else
43  tmp_token->text = NULL;
44 
45  return tmp_token;
46  }

50 getCurrentFilename()

55  string filename;

58  if (astIncludeStack.size() <= 1)

71  else

78  return filename;

82 setSourcePosition( SgLocatedNode* locatedNode )
83  {
84  // This function sets the source position to be marked as not available (since we often don't have token information)
85  // These nodes WILL be unparsed in the code generation phase.
86 
87  // The SgLocatedNode has both a startOfConstruct and endOfConstruct source position.
88  ROSE_ASSERT(locatedNode != NULL);
89 
90  // Make sure we never try to reset the source position of the global scope (set elsewhere in ROSE).
91  ROSE_ASSERT(isSgGlobal(locatedNode) == NULL);
92 
93  // Check the endOfConstruct first since it is most likely NULL (helpful in debugging)
94  if (locatedNode->get_endOfConstruct() != NULL || locatedNode->get_startOfConstruct() != NULL)
95  {
96  printf ("In setSourcePosition(SgLocatedNode* locatedNode): locatedNode = %p = %s \n",locatedNode,locatedNode->class_name().c_str());
97  }
98  ROSE_ASSERT(locatedNode->get_endOfConstruct() == NULL);
99  ROSE_ASSERT(locatedNode->get_startOfConstruct() == NULL);
100 
101  // DQ (2/25/2013): Use the SageInterface::setSourcePosition() function since it is the interface
102  // into the source position support in SageInterface. This makes the use consistant with that of
103  // the new C11/C++11 work.
104  // Call a mechanism defined in the SageInterface support
105  // SageInterface::setSourcePosition(locatedNode);
106  // Liao, 11/12/2012. The semantics of SageInterface::setSourcePosition() has changed, which now relies on an internal model variable
107  // (default to transformation generated file info, which does not fit to this context).
108  // So we directly use the real function we want: set to default position info.
109  // SageInterface::setSourcePositionToDefault(locatedNode);
110  SageInterface::setSourcePosition(locatedNode);
111  }

545  sourceLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct()->display("get_line() == 0: debug");
546 #endif
547  }
548  // DQ (3/4/2013): We can't assert this since it fails to some test codes (e.g. test2010_120.f90).
549  // ROSE_ASSERT(sourceLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct()->get_line() != 0);
550 
551  // Remove the existing Sg_File_Info objects, they will be reset below
552  delete targetLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct();
553  delete targetLocatedNode->get_endOfConstruct();
554 
555  // This is required to handle both the Fortran specific "include" files and the CPP specific "#include" files.
556  string filename = getCurrentFilename();
557  // printf ("In resetSourcePosition(%p = %s) filename = %s \n",targetLocatedNode,targetLocatedNode->class_name().c_str(),filename.c_str());
558  ROSE_ASSERT(filename.empty() == false);
559 
560  // Set these based on the source position information from the tokens
561  // locatedNode->set_startOfConstruct (new Sg_File_Info(*(firstToken->get_startOfConstruct())));
562  // locatedNode->set_endOfConstruct (new Sg_File_Info(*(lastToken ->get_endOfConstruct ())));
563  targetLocatedNode->set_startOfConstruct (new Sg_File_Info(*(sourceLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct())));
564  targetLocatedNode->set_endOfConstruct (new Sg_File_Info(*(sourceLocatedNode->get_endOfConstruct ())));
565 
566  targetLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct()->set_parent(targetLocatedNode);
567  targetLocatedNode->get_endOfConstruct ()->set_parent(targetLocatedNode);
568 
569  // DQ (2/15/2013): Added support to set the operatorPosition source position consistantly.
570  SgExpression* expression = isSgExpression(targetLocatedNode);
571  if (expression != NULL)
572  {
573  ROSE_ASSERT(expression->get_operatorPosition() != NULL);
574  // expression->get_operatorPosition()->updateSourcePosition(targetLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct());
575  *(expression->get_operatorPosition()) = *(targetLocatedNode->get_startOfConstruct());
576  }
577  }

579 // void resetEndingSourcePosition( SgLocatedNode* targetLocatedNode, Token_t* token )
580 void
581 resetEndingSourcePosition( SgLocatedNode* targetLocatedNode, Token_t* token )
582  {
583  // DQ (10/10/2010): This function is added to support resetting the end
584  // of the blocks (required to get comments woven into the AST properly).
585  ROSE_ASSERT(token != NULL);
586  int newLineNumber = token->line;
587 #if 0
588  printf ("Resetting the end of the target statement = %s to line = %d \n",targetLocatedNode->class_name().c_str(),newLineNumber);
589 #endif
590  resetEndingSourcePosition(targetLocatedNode,newLineNumber);
591 
592  SgFunctionDefinition* functionDefinition = isSgFunctionDefinition(targetLocatedNode);
593  if (functionDefinition != NULL)
594  {
595  // Also set the ending position of the function declaration.
596  // printf ("In resetEndingSourcePosition(): Set the ending position of the related function declaration \n");
597  SgDeclarationStatement* functionDeclaration = functionDefinition->get_declaration();
598  ROSE_ASSERT(functionDeclaration != NULL);
599  resetEndingSourcePosition(functionDeclaration,token);
600  }
601 
602  // Liao 2/1/2010. The SgBasicBlock of a SgFortranDo has to be adjusted also
603  // 1. the begin construct should be the same as the one of its first child statement
604  // 2. the end construct should be the same as SgFortranDo's end of construct
605  // This is the fix to bug 495: https://outreach.scidac.gov/tracker/index.php?func=detail&aid=495&group_id=24&atid=185
606  SgFortranDo * f_do = isSgFortranDo(targetLocatedNode);
607  if (f_do != NULL)
608  {
609  SgBasicBlock * body = f_do->get_body();
610  ROSE_ASSERT (body != NULL);
611  // adjust the startOfConstruct
612  SgStatementPtrList stmt_list = body->get_statements();
613  if (stmt_list.size()>0)
614  {
615  SgStatement* first_stmt = stmt_list[0];
616  ROSE_ASSERT(first_stmt !=NULL);
617  body->get_startOfConstruct()->set_filename(first_stmt->get_startOfConstruct()->get_filename());
618  body->get_startOfConstruct()->set_line(first_stmt->get_startOfConstruct()->get_line());
619  body->get_startOfConstruct()->set_col(first_stmt->get_startOfConstruct()->get_col());
620  }
621  // adjust the endOfConstruct:
622  // BTW. c_action_block () also tries to reset the end construct for the block.
623  // But the line number set here can be larger than the new line number c_action_block () tries to set and
624  // the larger one will be kept.
625  body->get_endOfConstruct()->set_filename(f_do->get_endOfConstruct()->get_filename());
626  body->get_endOfConstruct()->set_line(f_do->get_endOfConstruct()->get_line());
627  body->get_endOfConstruct()->set_col(f_do->get_endOfConstruct()->get_col());
628 
629  }
630 
631  // If this is the top level scope then iterate over the outer scopes to reset the end of each scope on the stack.
632  if (astScopeStack.front() == targetLocatedNode)
633  {
634  list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator i = astScopeStack.begin();
635  ROSE_ASSERT(targetLocatedNode == *i);
636  while (i != astScopeStack.end())
637  {
638 #if 0
639  printf ("In resetEndingSourcePosition(): Resetting the end of the block = %s to line = %d and file = %s \n",(*i)->class_name().c_str(),newLineNumber,getCurrentFilename().c_str());
640 #endif
641  resetEndingSourcePosition(*i,newLineNumber);
642 
643  ROSE_ASSERT((*i)->isCaseInsensitive() == true);
644 
645  i++;
646  }
647  }
648  }
649 
650 void resetEndingSourcePosition( SgLocatedNode* targetLocatedNode, SgStatement* sourceStatement )
651  {
652  // If this is not the same file then the line numbers will not make any sense.
653  ROSE_ASSERT(targetLocatedNode->get_endOfConstruct() != NULL);
654  ROSE_ASSERT(sourceStatement->get_endOfConstruct() != NULL);
655  if (targetLocatedNode->get_endOfConstruct()->isSameFile(sourceStatement->get_endOfConstruct()) == true)
656  {
657  int newLineNumber = sourceStatement->get_endOfConstruct()->get_line();
658  resetEndingSourcePosition(targetLocatedNode,newLineNumber);
659  }
660  else
661  {
662  // Increment the position by "1" since we have at least processed a Fortran include file on it's one line.
663 #if 0
664  printf ("Processing special case of source statement not in same file as the start of the scope. \n");
665 #endif
666  resetEndingSourcePosition(astScopeStack.front(),astScopeStack.front()->get_endOfConstruct()->get_line()+1);
667  }
668  }

739 SgType*
740 createType(int typeCode)
741  {
742  // This builds SgType IR nodes given the type code as input.
743  SgType* result = NULL;
744  switch(typeCode)
745  {
746  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_INTEGER: result = SgTypeInt::createType(); break;
747  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_REAL: result = SgTypeFloat::createType(); break;
748  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_DOUBLEPRECISION: result = SgTypeDouble::createType(); break;
749  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_DOUBLECOMPLEX: result = SgTypeComplex::createType(SgTypeDouble::createType()); break;
750  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_COMPLEX: result = SgTypeComplex::createType(SgTypeFloat::createType()); break;
751  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_CHARACTER: result = SgTypeChar::createType(); break;
752  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_LOGICAL: result = SgTypeBool::createType(); break;
753 
754  // Rice CAF types
755  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_TEAM: result = SgTypeCAFTeam::createType(); break;
756  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_CRAYPOINTER: result = SgTypeCrayPointer::createType(); break;
757  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_TOPOLOGY: result = SgTypeInt::createType(); break;
758  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_EVENT:
759  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_LOCK:
760  case IntrinsicTypeSpec_LOCKSET:
761  {
762  // TEMPORARY: need to add additional Rice type nodes to IR
763  SgIntVal * kind = new SgIntVal(8, "8");
764  setSourcePosition(kind);
765  result = SgTypeComplex::createType(SgTypeDouble::createType(kind));
766  break;
767  }
768 
769  default:
770  {
771  printf ("Default reached in createType: typeCode = %d \n",typeCode);
772  ROSE_ABORT();
773  }
774  }
775 
776  ROSE_ASSERT(result != NULL);
777  return result;
778  }

781 SgExpression*
782 createUnaryOperator ( SgExpression* exp, string name, bool is_user_defined_operator )
783  {
784  ROSE_ASSERT(exp != NULL);
785  SgExpression* result = NULL;
786 
787  // DQ (10/9/2008): Added support for user defined operators
788  if (is_user_defined_operator == true)
789  {
790  // Get the function symbol for the function defined by "name"
791  SgScopeStatement* currentScope = astScopeStack.front();
792 
793  // The name in the symbol table uses the form:
794  name = "operator(" + name + ")";
795 #if 0
796  printf ("name = %s \n",name.c_str());
797  printf ("currentScope = %p = %s \n",currentScope,currentScope->class_name().c_str());
798 #endif
799  // currentScope->print_symboltable ("In createBinaryOperator()");
800 
801  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol(name,currentScope);
802  ROSE_ASSERT(functionSymbol != NULL);
803 
804  result = new SgUserDefinedUnaryOp(exp,NULL,name,functionSymbol);
805 
806  ROSE_ASSERT(result != NULL);
807  return result;
808  }
809 
810  int stringLength = name.length();
811  if (stringLength == 1)
812  {
813  switch (name[0])
814  {
815  case '!':
816  {
817  // printf ("Building a SgLessThanOp binary operator \n");
818  result = new SgNotOp(exp,NULL);
819  break;
820  }
821 
822  default:
823  {
824  printf ("Error: default reached relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
825  ROSE_ABORT();
826  }
827  }
828  }
829  else
830  {
831  // ROSE_ASSERT(stringLength == 2);
832  if (stringLength == 2)
833  {
834  // Not sure what these would be.
835  printf ("2 character unary operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
836  ROSE_ABORT();
837  }
838  else
839  {
840  if (stringLength == 4)
841  {
842  if (matchingName(name,".XX.") == true)
843  {
844  }
845  else
846  {
847  printf ("Error: not sure what the operator is: %s \n",name.c_str());
848  ROSE_ABORT();
849  }
850  }
851  else
852  {
853  if (stringLength == 5)
854  {
855  // This is the case for ".OR." etc.
856  if (matchingName(name,".NOT.") == true)
857  {
858  result = new SgNotOp(exp,NULL);
859  }
860  else
861  {
862  printf ("n != 1,2,4,5 character operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
863  ROSE_ABORT();
864  }
865  }
866  }
867  }
868  }
869 
870  ROSE_ASSERT(result != NULL);
871  return result;
872  }

874 SgExpression*
875 createBinaryOperator ( SgExpression* lhs, SgExpression* rhs, string name, bool is_user_defined_operator )
876  {
877  ROSE_ASSERT(lhs != NULL);
878  ROSE_ASSERT(rhs != NULL);
879  SgExpression* result = NULL;
880 
881  // DQ (10/9/2008): Added support for user defined operators
882  if (is_user_defined_operator == true)
883  {
884  // Get the function symbol for the function defined by "name"
885  SgScopeStatement* currentScope = astScopeStack.front();
886 #if 0
887  printf ("name = %s \n",name.c_str());
888  printf ("currentScope = %p = %s \n",currentScope,currentScope->class_name().c_str());
889 #endif
890  // currentScope->print_symboltable ("In createBinaryOperator()");
891 
892  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol(name,currentScope);
893  ROSE_ASSERT(functionSymbol != NULL);
894 
895  result = new SgUserDefinedBinaryOp(lhs,rhs,NULL,name,functionSymbol);
896 
897  ROSE_ASSERT(result != NULL);
898  return result;
899  }
900 
901  int stringLength = name.length();
902  if (stringLength == 1)
903  {
904  switch (name[0])
905  {
906  case '<':
907  {
908  // printf ("Building a SgLessThanOp binary operator \n");
909  result = new SgLessThanOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
910  break;
911  }
912 
913  case '>':
914  {
915  // printf ("Building a SgLessThanOp binary operator \n");
916  result = new SgGreaterThanOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
917  break;
918  }
919 
920  default:
921  {
922  printf ("Error: default reached relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
923  ROSE_ABORT();
924  }
925  }
926  }
927  else
928  {
929  // ROSE_ASSERT(stringLength == 2);
930  if (stringLength == 2)
931  {
932  // This is likely the case of ">=", "<=", "/=", "=="
933  // printf ("2 character operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
934  // ROSE_ABORT();
935 
936  if (name == "<=")
937  {
938  result = new SgLessOrEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
939  }
940  else
941  {
942  if (name == ">=")
943  {
944  result = new SgGreaterOrEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
945  }
946  else
947  {
948  if (name == "==")
949  {
950  result = new SgEqualityOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
951  }
952  else
953  {
954  // In C this would be the "!=" operator, in fortran it is "/="
955  if (name == "/=")
956  {
957  result = new SgNotEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
958  }
959  else
960  {
961  if (name == "//")
962  {
963  result = new SgConcatenationOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
964  }
965  else
966  {
967  printf ("2 character operator not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
968  ROSE_ABORT();
969  }
970  }
971  }
972  }
973  }
974  }
975  else
976  {
977  if (stringLength == 4)
978  {
979  // These are all case insensitive.
980  // This is the case for ".LT.", ".LE.", ".EQ.", ".NE.", ".GT.", ".GE.", and ".OR." etc.
981  if (matchingName(name,".LT.") == true)
982  {
983  result = new SgLessThanOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
984  }
985  else
986  {
987  if (matchingName(name,".LE.") == true)
988  {
989  result = new SgLessOrEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
990  }
991  else
992  {
993  if (matchingName(name,".EQ.") == true)
994  {
995  result = new SgEqualityOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
996  }
997  else
998  {
999  if (matchingName(name,".NE.") == true)
1000  {
1001  result = new SgNotEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1002  }
1003  else
1004  {
1005  if (matchingName(name,".GT.") == true)
1006  {
1007  result = new SgGreaterThanOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1008  }
1009  else
1010  {
1011  if (matchingName(name,".GE.") == true)
1012  {
1013  result = new SgGreaterOrEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1014  }
1015  else
1016  {
1017  if (matchingName(name,".OR.") == true)
1018  {
1019  result = new SgOrOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1020  }
1021  else
1022  {
1023  printf ("4 character operator not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
1024  ROSE_ABORT();
1025  }
1026  }
1027  }
1028  }
1029  }
1030  }
1031  }
1032  }
1033  else
1034  {
1035  if (stringLength == 5)
1036  {
1037  // These are all case insensitive.
1038  // This is the case for ".AND." etc.
1039  if (matchingName(name,".AND.") == true)
1040  {
1041  result = new SgAndOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1042  }
1043  else
1044  {
1045  if (matchingName(name,".EQV.") == true)
1046  {
1047  result = new SgEqualityOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1048  }
1049  else
1050  {
1051  printf ("n != 2,4,5 character operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
1052  ROSE_ABORT();
1053  }
1054  }
1055  }
1056  else
1057  {
1058  if (stringLength == 6)
1059  {
1060  // This is the case for ".NEQV." etc.
1061  if (matchingName(name,".NEQV.") == true)
1062  {
1063  // DQ (8/5/2010): This might output .NE. instead of .NEQV. and the two are .NEQV.!
1064  result = new SgNotEqualOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
1065  }
1066  else
1067  {
1068  printf ("n != 2,4,5,6 character operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
1069  ROSE_ABORT();
1070  }
1071  }
1072  }
1073  // printf ("n != 2,4 character operators not implemented relOp = %s \n",name.c_str());
1074  // ROSE_ASSERT(false);
1075  }
1076  }
1077  }
1078 
1079  ROSE_ASSERT(result != NULL);
1080  return result;
1081  }

1094 void outputState( const std::string label )
1095  {
1096  // This function is used for debugging and outputs the data in the different
1097  // stacks used to accumulate intermeditate data as part of building the AST.
1098  // Output the stack information for:
1099  // astScopeStack,
1100  // astExpressionStack,
1101  // astNodeStack,
1102  // astNameStack,
1103  // astTypeStack,
1104  // astIntentSpecStack,
1105  // astAttributeSpecStack,
1106  // astDeclarationStatementStack,
1107  // astInitializerStack,
1108 
1109  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() <= 2 )
1110  {
1111  // Skip output of stack data for verbose levels less than or equal to 2
1112  return;
1113  }
1114 
1115  size_t maxStackSize = astScopeStack.size();
1116  maxStackSize = astExpressionStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astExpressionStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1117  maxStackSize = astNodeStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astNodeStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1118  maxStackSize = astNameStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astNameStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1119  maxStackSize = astBaseTypeStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astBaseTypeStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1120  maxStackSize = astTypeStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astTypeStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1121  maxStackSize = astIntentSpecStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astIntentSpecStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1122  maxStackSize = astAttributeSpecStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astAttributeSpecStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1123  // maxStackSize = astInitializerStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astInitializerStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1124  maxStackSize = astTypeKindStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astTypeKindStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1125  maxStackSize = astTypeParameterStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astTypeParameterStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1126  maxStackSize = astLabelSymbolStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astLabelSymbolStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1127 
1128  // maxStackSize = astDeclarationStatementStack.size() > maxStackSize ? astDeclarationStatementStack.size() : maxStackSize;
1129

1367 SgScopeStatement* getTopOfScopeStack()
1368  {

1378  // Testing the scope stack...
1379  // DQ (11/28/2010): Added specification of case insensitivity for Fortran.

1382  {
1383  if ((*scopeInterator)->isCaseInsensitive() == false)
1384  {
1385  printf ("##### Error: the scope handling is set to case sensitive scopeInterator = %p = %s \n",*scopeInterator,(*scopeInterator)->class_name().c_str());
1386  // (*scopeInterator)->setCaseInsensitive(true);
1387  }
1388  ROSE_ASSERT((*scopeInterator)->isCaseInsensitive() == true);
1389  scopeInterator++;
1390  }
1391 
1392  return topOfStack;
1393  }

1434 SgExpression*
1435 buildLabelRefExp(SgExpression* expression)
1436  {
1437  SgExpression* returnExpression = expression;
1438 
1439  // If this is an integer it is a format label and we want to generate a SgLabelRefExp
1440  SgIntVal* integerValue = isSgIntVal(expression);
1441  if (integerValue != NULL)
1442  {
1443  // If this is an integer, then generate a SgLabelRefExp.
1444  SgName name = StringUtility::numberToString(integerValue->get_value());
1445 
1446  Token_t* format_label = create_token(1,0,0,name.str());
1447  SgLabelSymbol* labelSymbol = buildNumericLabelSymbol(format_label);
1448 
1449  // DQ (11/5/2016): The token support is using C style malloc, so we need to use C style free to be consistant.
1450  // delete format_label;
1451  free(format_label);
1452 
1453  format_label = NULL;
1454 
1455  labelSymbol->set_label_type(SgLabelSymbol::e_start_label_type);
1456 
1457  SgLabelRefExp* labelRefExp = new SgLabelRefExp(labelSymbol);
1458  // printf ("################## In buildLabelRefExp(): labelRefExp = %p value = %d \n",labelRefExp,labelRefExp->get_symbol()->get_numeric_label_value());
1459 
1460  setSourcePosition(labelRefExp);
1461 
1462  // DQ (1/26/2009): Set the parent of the SgIntVal IR node.
1463  integerValue->set_parent(labelRefExp);
1464 
1465  returnExpression = labelRefExp;
1466  }
1467 
1468  return returnExpression;
1469  }

1473 getFunctionDefinitionFromScopeStack()

1476  SgFunctionDefinition* functionDefinition = NULL;
1477 
1478  std::list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator i = astScopeStack.begin();
1479  // printf ("Defining iterator i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1480 
1481  while ( i != astScopeStack.end() && isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) == NULL )
1482  {
1483  // printf ("Looping iterator (before ++) i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1484  i++;

1498 SgLabelSymbol*
1499 buildNumericLabelSymbol(Token_t* label)
1500  {
1501  // This is the function we use to create the label that might refer to a
1502  // previously seen statement or a statement we will see in the future.
1503 
1504  ASSERT_not_null(label);
1505  ASSERT_not_null(label->text);
1506 
1507  // DQ (11/22/2010): This is a bug in OFP, but I have to work around it for now.
1508  if (label->line == 0)
1509  {
1510  printf ("Error (OFP bug): label->line == 0 for label->text = %s \n",label->text);
1511  }
1512 
1513  SgLabelSymbol* returnSymbol = nullptr;
1514 
1515 #if 0
1516  // Output debugging information about saved state (stack) information.
1517  outputState("At TOP of buildNumericLabelSymbol()");
1518 #endif
1519 
1520  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL ) {
1521  printf ("This code can be replaced with a call to getFunctionDefinitionFromScopeStack() \n");
1522  }
1523 
1524  std::list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator i = astScopeStack.begin();
1525  // printf ("Defining iterator i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1526  // while ( astScopeStack.empty() == false && i != astScopeStack.end() && isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) == NULL )
1527  while ( i != astScopeStack.end() && isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) == NULL )
1528  {
1529  // printf ("Looping iterator (before ++) i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1530  i++;
1531  // printf ("Looping iterator i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1532  }
1533 
1534  // A label on a program statement will not have a scope in which to be identified. "10 program main"
1535  // It is not clear what scope such a label should be added (global scope?).
1536  if (i != astScopeStack.end())
1537  {
1538  // printf ("Looking for SgLabelSymbol i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1539  ASSERT_not_null(isSgFunctionDefinition(*i));
1540 
1541  SgName name = label->text;
1542  returnSymbol = (*i)->lookup_label_symbol(name);
1543 
1544  // printf ("In buildNumericLabelSymbol(): returnSymbol = %p \n",returnSymbol);
1545  if (returnSymbol == nullptr)
1546  {
1547  // The symbol was not found, create a symbol so that statements can reference
1548  // it then we can fixup the statement in the symbol later (when we see it).
1549  int label_value = atoi(label->text);
1550  // printf ("Building a SgLabelSymbol for a numeric label that we have not see yet: label_value = %d = %s \n",label_value,label->text);
1551 
1552  returnSymbol = new SgLabelSymbol((SgLabelStatement*) nullptr);
1553  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
1554  returnSymbol->set_fortran_statement(nullptr);
1555  returnSymbol->set_numeric_label_value(label_value);
1556 
1557  SgStatement* label_statement = new SgNullStatement();
1558  // printf ("Building SgNullStatement label_statement = %p \n",label_statement);
1559 
1560  returnSymbol->set_fortran_statement(label_statement);
1561 
1562  // DQ (1/20/2008): The parent of a statement can't be set to a SgSymbol, so make it point to the current scope for now!
1563  // label_statement->set_parent(returnSymbol);
1564  label_statement->set_parent(astScopeStack.front());
1565  ASSERT_not_null(label_statement->get_parent());
1566 
1567  // DQ (1/20/2008): If the label is not present, but is referenced then this has to be set.
1568  // Note that test2007_175.f demonstrates that if the lable is not present
1569  // then this label_statement fails because the source position is not set.
1570  setSourcePosition(label_statement);
1571 
1572  ASSERT_not_null(isSgFunctionDefinition(*i));
1573  // Insert the symbol into the function definition's symbol table so it will be found next time.
1574  (*i)->insert_symbol(name,returnSymbol);
1575  }
1576 
1577  ROSE_ASSERT(returnSymbol != NULL);
1578  }
1579  else
1580  {
1581  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
1582  printf ("WARNING: label attached to construct not in a function scope! \n");
1583 #if 0
1584  // Output debugging information about saved state (stack) information.
1585  outputState("WARNING: At BOTTOM of buildNumericLabelSymbol()");
1586 #endif
1587  }
1588 
1589  // printf ("Returning from buildNumericLabelSymbol() returnSymbol = %p \n",returnSymbol);
1590  return returnSymbol;
1591  }

1593 SgLabelSymbol*
1594 buildNumericLabelSymbolAndAssociateWithStatement(SgStatement* stmt, Token_t* label)
1595  {
1596  // This is the function we use to associate a label with a statement.
1597  // The label may be been previously build if there was a forward
1598  // reference to the statement's label. This might also be the label for
1599  // the statements asociated end of construct (for the label associated
1600  // with "end" for example).
1601 
1602  ROSE_ASSERT(label != NULL);
1603  // ROSE_ASSERT(label->line > 0);
1604  ROSE_ASSERT(label->line >= 0); // DXN: FIXME - workaround OFP bug where label->line = 0 as in the following example:
1605  /* subroutine FOURT()
1606  * DO 125 I1=1, 2
1607  * DO 125 I3= 3, 4
1608  * 125 CONTINUE
1609  * END
1610  *
1611  * When label is parsed the second time around, label->line = 0 and label->col = -1
1612  */
1613  ROSE_ASSERT(label->text != NULL);
1614 
1615  // Assumes simple string based representation of integer
1616  // I used atoi(), even though strtol() is suggested. We store the
1617  // numeric lables in the AST as numeric values.
1618  // int numericLabel = atoi(label->text);
1619  // printf ("label->text = %s numericLabel = %d \n",label->text,numericLabel);
1620  // stmt->set_numeric_label(numericLabel);
1621 
1622  std::list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator i = astScopeStack.begin();
1623  // printf ("Starting at the scope = %s \n",(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1624 
1625  // DQ (12/9/2007): Added support for numeric lables to be SgLabelSymbols.
1626  // It is unclear if we want to use the function scope of the global scope
1627  // (I have use the function scope, where the function is not explicit this
1628  // is still using the compiler generated function).
1629  while ( i != astScopeStack.end() && isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) == NULL )
1630  {
1631  i++;
1632  }
1633 
1634  ROSE_ASSERT( i != astScopeStack.end() );
1635  ROSE_ASSERT(isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) != NULL);
1636 
1637  // printf ("Looking for SgLabelSymbol i scope = %p = %s \n",*i,(*i)->class_name().c_str());
1638 
1639  SgName name = label->text;
1640  SgLabelSymbol* label_symbol = (*i)->lookup_label_symbol(name);
1641  if (label_symbol == NULL)
1642  {
1643  // If this does not exist then build the associated label symbol and put it into the function's symbol table.
1644  label_symbol = new SgLabelSymbol((SgLabelStatement*) NULL);
1645  label_symbol->set_fortran_statement(stmt);
1646 
1647  // DQ (12/24/2007): The new design stores the numeric label value in the SgLabelSymbol.
1648  int label_value = atoi(label->text);
1649  // printf ("Building a SgLabelSymbol for a numeric label that we have not see yet: label_value = %d = %s \n",label_value,label->text);
1650  label_symbol->set_numeric_label_value(label_value);
1651 
1652  // printf ("Warning in buildNumericLabelSymbolAndAssociateWithStatement(): setting label_type using SgLabelSymbol::e_end_label_type \n");
1653  label_symbol->set_label_type(SgLabelSymbol::e_end_label_type);
1654 
1655  ROSE_ASSERT(isSgFunctionDefinition(*i) != NULL);
1656  (*i)->insert_symbol(name,label_symbol);
1657 
1658  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
1659  printf ("Built a new SgLabelSymbol = %p (numeric value = %d) for name = %s associated with statement %p \n",label_symbol,label_value,name.str(),stmt);
1660  }
1661  else
1662  {
1663  // If this exists then it was build with a SgNullStatement and we have to replace the statement.
1664  SgStatement* tempStatement = label_symbol->get_fortran_statement();
1665 
1666  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
1667  printf ("Found an existing SgLabelSymbol = %p for name = %s associated with statement %p (deleted tempStatement = %p) \n",label_symbol,name.str(),stmt,tempStatement);
1668 
1669  // DQ (12/24/2007): New implementation does not use SgNullStatement internally. NOT TRUE, we need these for forward references to numeric labels.
1670  // ROSE_ASSERT(isSgNullStatement(tempStatement) == NULL);
1671 
1672  // DQ (12/24/2007): If this is associated with a SgFortranDo statement, then don't delete it.
1673  // Only delete it if it is a SgNullStatement. This should solve the problem with test2007_233.f
1674  // (fixed this problem, but not finished yet).
1675  if (isSgNullStatement(tempStatement) != NULL)
1676  {
1677  delete tempStatement;
1678  tempStatement = NULL;
1679  }
1680  label_symbol->set_fortran_statement(NULL);
1681  label_symbol->set_fortran_statement(stmt);

1903 setStatementStringLabel(SgStatement* stmt, Token_t* label)

1906  {

1908  ROSE_ASSERT(label->text != NULL);
1909 
1910  // Note that an alternative to this switch would be to have the
1911  // apropriate virtual dunctioned defined in the IR nodes.
1912  switch (stmt->variantT())
1913  {
1914  case V_SgWhereStatement:
1915  {
1916  SgWhereStatement* statement = isSgWhereStatement(stmt);
1917  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1918  break;
1919  }
1920 
1921  case V_SgFortranDo:
1922  {
1923  SgFortranDo* statement = isSgFortranDo(stmt);
1924  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1925  break;
1926  }
1927 
1928  case V_SgIfStmt:
1929  {
1930  SgIfStmt* statement = isSgIfStmt(stmt);
1931  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1932  break;
1933  }
1934 
1935  case V_SgForStatement:
1936  {
1937  SgForStatement* statement = isSgForStatement(stmt);
1938  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1939  break;
1940  }
1941 
1942  case V_SgSwitchStatement:
1943  {
1944  SgSwitchStatement* statement = isSgSwitchStatement(stmt);
1945  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1946  break;
1947  }
1948 
1949  case V_SgWhileStmt:
1950  {
1951  SgWhileStmt* statement = isSgWhileStmt(stmt);
1952  statement->set_string_label(label->text);
1953  break;
1954  }
1955 
1956  default:
1957  {
1958  printf ("Error: set_string_label() not defined for this statement = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
1959  ROSE_ABORT();
1960  }
1961  }
1962  }
1963  }

1969  // This function traces back through the parent scopes to search for the named module symbol in an outer scope

1989  SgScopeStatement* tempScope = currentScope;
1990 
1991  // DQ (12/12/2007): Added test for if this is a function!

2005  // This function could have returned a NULL pointer if there was no symbol found ???
2006  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )

2094 SgVariableSymbol*
2095 trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(const SgName & variableName, SgScopeStatement* currentScope )
2096  {
2097  // This function traces back through the parent scopes to search for the named symbol in an outer scope
2098  // Semantics of this function:
2099  // It returns NULL if the named variable is not found in any scope.
2100  // If the variable should be implicitly defined then it is built, but the function still returns NULL.
2101  // Note that this means that using it to get the symbol for an implicitly defined variable that has not
2102  // been used required calling the function twice.
2103 
2104  // Whe looking at scopes this function does not look in any scopes specified using a
2105  // C++ using declaration (SgUsingDeclarationStatement), using directives (SgUsingDirectiveStatement), a
2106  // Fortran use statement (SgUseStatement). This is handled by having SgAliasSymbol to represent such
2107  // symbols that have been imported into the associated scope of the using declarations (or use statement
2108  // in fortran).
2109 
2110 #if 0
2111  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
2112  printf ("In trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(): variableName = %s currentScope = %p \n",variableName.str(),currentScope);
2113 #endif

2116  // (see test2007_213.f, if so then this can be one of the first c_action statements called.
2117  // build_implicit_program_statement_if_required();
2118 
2119  SgVariableSymbol* variableSymbol = NULL;
2120  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = NULL;
2121  SgClassSymbol* classSymbol = NULL;

2123  // trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol_but_do_not_build_variable(variableName,currentScope,variableSymbol,functionSymbol);
2124  trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol_but_do_not_build_variable(variableName,currentScope,variableSymbol,functionSymbol,classSymbol);
2125 
2126 #if 0
2127  printf ("In trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(): variableSymbol = %p \n",variableSymbol);
2128  printf ("In trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(): functionSymbol = %p \n",functionSymbol);
2129  printf ("In trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(): classSymbol = %p \n",classSymbol);
2130 #endif

2132 #if 0
2133  printf ("Output the symbol table at the current scope (debugging): \n");
2134  currentScope->get_symbol_table()->print("Output the symbol table at the current scope");
2135 #endif
2136 
2137  if ( (variableSymbol == NULL) && functionSymbol == NULL && classSymbol == NULL && (matchAgainstIntrinsicFunctionList(variableName.str()) == false) )
2138  {
2139  // FMZ(1/8/2010)
2140  // if the Id name is "team_world" or "team_default", generate team,external:: declarations
2141  {
2142  string teamName = variableName.str();
2143  std::transform(teamName.begin(),teamName.end(),teamName.begin(),::tolower);
2144

2146  string teamDefault = "team_default";

2148  {
2149  return add_external_team_decl(teamName);

2153  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
2154  printf ("Warning: trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol(): could not locate the specified variable (for %s) in any outer symbol table: astNameStack.size() = %" PRIuPTR " \n",variableName.str(),astNameStack.size());
2155  // printf ("astNameStack.front() = %p = %s = %s \n",astNameStack.front(),astNameStack.front()->class_name().c_str(),SageInterface::get_name(astNameStack.front()).c_str());
2156 
2157  if (astNameStack.empty() == false)

2160  printf ("astNameStack.front() = %p = %s \n",astNameStack.front(),astNameStack.front()->text);
2161  }

2163  // Check if this is a scope using implicit none rules, however for now even if we know it is function we
2164  // first build it as a variable and later convert it to either an array or a function (or a derived type).
2165  bool isAnImplicitNoneScope = isImplicitNoneScope();
2166  if (isAnImplicitNoneScope == true)
2167  {
2168  // This has to be a function call since we can't be building a variable to represent an implicitly type variable.
2169  // See jacobi.f for an example of this. Also, currently test2010_45.f90 demonstrates a case of "integer x = 42, y = x"
2170  // where the initializer to "y" is not built as a symbol yet as part of the construction of the variable declaration.
2171 #if 0

2175  // Or we could define a list of unresolved functions and fix them up at the end of the module or global scope. This is a general problem
2176  // and demonstrated by test2010_46.f90
2177  if (astNameStack.empty() != false)
2178  cerr << "Error: name stack is empty when handling variable:"<<variableName.str() << endl;

2196  setSourcePosition(functionDeclaration);

2198 
2199  ROSE_ASSERT(functionDeclaration->get_endOfConstruct() != NULL);

2247  // printf ("Adding function name = %s to the global scope (even though we have not seen the definition yet) \n",name.str());

2250  // Add this function to the list of unresolved functions so that we can fixup the AST afterward (close of module scope or close of global scope).

2252 #if 0
2253  printf ("Error: scope marked as implict none, so we must construct name = %s as a function (function reference expression) \n",variableName.str());
2254  ROSE_ABORT();
2255 #endif
2256  }
2257  else
2258  {
2259  // printf ("NOTE: CANCLED SEMANTICS THAT BUILD IMPLICIT VARIABLE SYMBOLS \n");
2260  }
2261  }
2262 
2263 #if 0

2757  // classDeclaration->set_endOfConstruct(SOURCE_POSITION);

2760  // setSourcePosition(classDeclaration);

2773  nondefiningClassDeclaration->set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(nondefiningClassDeclaration);

2820  assert(classDeclaration->get_definition() != NULL);

2952 bool
2953 isImplicitNoneScope()
2954  {
2955  // This function works by traversing the scopes to the SgFunctionDefinition scope and looking
2956  // for an implicit none statement. We can make this more efficient at a later point.
2957 
2958  // Default is that we are NOT in an implicit none scope.
2959  bool isImplicitNoneScope = false;
2960 
2961  // DQ (12/10/2016): Eliminating a warning that we want to be an error: -Werror=unused-but-set-variable.
2962  // bool foundFunctionDefinition = false;
2963 
2964  std::list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator i = astScopeStack.begin();
2965  while ( i != astScopeStack.end() )
2966  {
2967  // Find the function definition, or where else an implicit statement can be!
2968  // module statement, interface statement
2969 
2970  SgFunctionDefinition* functionDefinition = isSgFunctionDefinition(*i);
2971  if (functionDefinition != NULL)
2972  {
2973  // DQ (12/10/2016): Eliminating a warning that we want to be an error: -Werror=unused-but-set-variable.
2974  // foundFunctionDefinition = true;
2975  std::vector<SgStatement*>::iterator j = functionDefinition->get_body()->get_statements().begin();
2976  while ( j != functionDefinition->get_body()->get_statements().end() )
2977  {
2978  // Look for the SgImplicitStatement, then test if it was specificed using "none"
2979  SgImplicitStatement* implicitStatement = isSgImplicitStatement(*j);
2980  if (implicitStatement != NULL && implicitStatement->get_implicit_none() == true)
2981  isImplicitNoneScope = true;
2982 
2983  j++;
2984  }
2985  }
2986  // Pei-Hung (07/25/2019) search for implicit statement in modules
2987  SgClassDefinition* classDefinition = isSgClassDefinition(*i);
2988  if (classDefinition != NULL)
2989  {
2990  SgDeclarationStatementPtrList& declStmtList = classDefinition->get_members();
2991  SgDeclarationStatementPtrList::const_iterator j = declStmtList.begin();
2992  while (j != declStmtList.end())
2993  {
2994  SgImplicitStatement* implicitStatement = isSgImplicitStatement(*j);
2995  if (implicitStatement != NULL && implicitStatement->get_implicit_none() == true)
2996  isImplicitNoneScope = true;
2997  j++;
2998  }
2999  }
3000  i++;
3001  }
3002 
3003  // DQ (5/21/2008): for the case of a module we will not find a SgFunctionDefinition (see test2008_35.f90)
3004  // ROSE_ASSERT(foundFunctionDefinition == true);
3005 
3006  return isImplicitNoneScope;
3007  }

3233  ROSE_ASSERT(lastInitializedNameForSourcePosition->get_startOfConstruct() != NULL);
3234  *(variableDeclaration->get_startOfConstruct()) = *(firstInitializedNameForSourcePosition->get_startOfConstruct());
3235  *(variableDeclaration->get_endOfConstruct()) = *(lastInitializedNameForSourcePosition->get_startOfConstruct());
3236 
3237  // DQ (12/1/2007): It is better to not clear the stack here and instead clear it in R501
3238 
3239  return variableDeclaration;
3240  }

3243 void
3244 initialize_global_scope_if_required()
3245  {
3246  // First we have to get the global scope initialized (and pushed onto the stack).
3247 
3248  // DQ (2/25/2013): Set the default for source position generation to be consistent with other languages (e.g. C/C++).
3249  SageBuilder::setSourcePositionClassificationMode(SageBuilder::e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction);
3250 
3251  // printf ("In initialize_global_scope_if_required(): astScopeStack.empty() = %s \n",astScopeStack.empty() ? "true" : "false");
3252  if (astScopeStack.empty() == true)
3253  {
3254  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
3255  printf ("In initialize_global_scope_if_required(): OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer = %p \n",OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer);
3256 
3257  ROSE_ASSERT(OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer != NULL);
3258  SgSourceFile* file = OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer;
3259  SgGlobal* globalScope = file->get_globalScope();
3260  ROSE_ASSERT(globalScope != NULL);
3261  ROSE_ASSERT(globalScope->get_parent() != NULL);
3262 
3263  // DQ (11/28/2010): Added specification of case insensitivity for Fortran.
3264  globalScope->setCaseInsensitive(true);
3265 
3266  // DQ (8/21/2008): endOfConstruct is not set to be consistant with startOfConstruct.
3267  ROSE_ASSERT(globalScope->get_endOfConstruct() != NULL);
3268  ROSE_ASSERT(globalScope->get_startOfConstruct() != NULL);
3269 
3270  // Scopes should be pushed onto the front of the stack (we define the top of the stack to
3271  // be the front). I have used a vector instead of a stack for now, this might change later.
3272  ROSE_ASSERT(astScopeStack.empty() == true);
3273  astScopeStack.push_front(globalScope);
3274 
3275  // DQ (10/10/2010): Set the start position of global scope to "1".
3276  globalScope->get_startOfConstruct()->set_line(1);
3277 
3278  // DQ (10/10/2010): Set this position to the same value so that if we increment
3279  // by "1" the start and end will not be the same value.
3280  globalScope->get_endOfConstruct()->set_line(1);
3281 #if 0
3282  astScopeStack.front()->get_startOfConstruct()->display("In initialize_global_scope_if_required(): start");
3283  astScopeStack.front()->get_endOfConstruct ()->display("In initialize_global_scope_if_required(): end");
3284 #endif
3285  }
3286 
3287  // Testing the scope stack...
3288  // DQ (11/28/2010): Added specification of case insensitivity for Fortran.
3289  std::list<SgScopeStatement*>::iterator scopeInterator = astScopeStack.begin();
3290  while (scopeInterator != astScopeStack.end())
3291  {
3292  if ((*scopeInterator)->isCaseInsensitive() == false)
3293  {
3294  printf ("##### Error (in initialize_global_scope_if_required): the scope handling is set to case sensitive scopeInterator = %p = %s \n",*scopeInterator,(*scopeInterator)->class_name().c_str());
3295  // (*scopeInterator)->setCaseInsensitive(true);
3296  }
3297  ROSE_ASSERT((*scopeInterator)->isCaseInsensitive() == true);
3298  scopeInterator++;
3299  }
3300  }

3302 bool
3303 matchingName ( string x, string y )
3304  {
3305  // This function checks a case insensitive match of x against y.
3306  // This is required because Fortran is case insensitive.
3307 
3308  size_t x_length = x.length();
3309  size_t y_length = y.length();
3310 
3311  return (x_length == y_length) ? strncasecmp(x.c_str(),y.c_str(),x_length) == 0 : false;
3312  }

3314 // bool matchAgainstImplicitFunctionList( std::string s )
3315 bool
3316 matchAgainstIntrinsicFunctionList( std::string s )
3317  {
3318  // This function should likely break out the subroutines and procedures that would be associated with a "call" statement.
3319 
3320  bool resultValue = false;
3321 
3322  // Need caseinsensitive version: strncasecmp(keyword1->text,"real",4) == 0
3323 
3324  // bool isTypeInqueryFunction = (s == "associated") || (s == "present") || (s == "kind");
3325  bool isTypeInqueryFunction = matchingName(s,"associated") || matchingName(s,"present") || matchingName(s,"kind");
3326 
3327  bool isElementalNumericFunction =
3328  matchingName(s,"abs") || matchingName(s,"aimag") || matchingName(s,"aint") || matchingName(s,"anint") || matchingName(s,"ceiling") ||
3329  matchingName(s,"cmplx") || matchingName(s,"floor") || matchingName(s,"int") || matchingName(s,"nint") || matchingName(s,"real");
3330 
3331  bool isElementalNonConversionFunction =
3332  matchingName(s,"conjg") || matchingName(s,"dim") || matchingName(s,"max") || matchingName(s,"min") || matchingName(s,"mod") || matchingName(s,"modulo") || matchingName(s,"sign");
3333 
3334  bool isElementalMathFunction =
3335  matchingName(s,"acos") || matchingName(s,"asin") || matchingName(s,"atan") || matchingName(s,"atan2") || matchingName(s,"cos") ||
3336  matchingName(s,"cosh") || matchingName(s,"exp") || matchingName(s,"log") || matchingName(s,"log10") || matchingName(s,"sin") ||
3337  matchingName(s,"sinh") || matchingName(s,"sqrt") || matchingName(s,"tan") || matchingName(s,"tanh");
3338 
3339  bool isCharacterConversionFunction =
3340  matchingName(s,"achar") || matchingName(s,"char") || matchingName(s,"iachar") || matchingName(s,"ichar");
3341 
3342  bool isLexicalCompareFunction = matchingName(s,"lge") || matchingName(s,"lgt") || matchingName(s,"lle") || matchingName(s,"llt");
3343 
3344  bool isStringHandlingElementalFunction =
3345  matchingName(s,"adjustl") || matchingName(s,"adjustr") || matchingName(s,"index") || matchingName(s,"len_trim") || matchingName(s,"scan") || matchingName(s,"verify");
3346 
3347  bool isLogicalConversionFunction = matchingName(s,"logical");
3348 
3349  bool isStringInqueryFunction = matchingName(s,"len");
3350 
3351  bool isStringTransformationFunction = matchingName(s,"repeat") || matchingName(s,"trim");
3352 
3353  bool isNumericInqueryFunction =
3354  matchingName(s,"digits") || matchingName(s,"epsilon") || matchingName(s,"huge") || matchingName(s,"maxexponent") || matchingName(s,"minexponent") || matchingName(s,"precision") || matchingName(s,"radix") || matchingName(s,"range") || matchingName(s,"tiny");
3355 
3356  bool isElementalRealFunction =
3357  matchingName(s,"exponent") || matchingName(s,"fraction") || matchingName(s,"nearest") || matchingName(s,"rrspacing") || matchingName(s,"scale") || matchingName(s,"set_exponent") || matchingName(s,"spacing");
3358 
3359  bool isKindTransformationFunction = matchingName(s,"selected_int_kind") || matchingName(s,"selected_real_kind");
3360 
3361  bool isBitInqueryFunction = matchingName(s,"bit_size");
3362 
3363  bool isBitElementalFunction =
3364  matchingName(s,"btest") || matchingName(s,"iand") || matchingName(s,"ibclr") || matchingName(s,"ibits") || matchingName(s,"ibset") || matchingName(s,"ieor") ||
3365  matchingName(s,"ior") || matchingName(s,"ishft") || matchingName(s,"ishftc") || matchingName(s,"not");
3366 
3367  // This is a procedure and so should be associated with a call statment and so it is different
3368  bool isBitElementalSubroutine = matchingName(s,"mvbits");
3369 
3370  bool isTransferFunction = matchingName(s,"transfer");
3371 
3372  bool isVectorMatrixMultipyFunction = matchingName(s,"dot_product") || matchingName(s,"matmul");
3373 
3374  // These can take one argument with an optional "dim" argument, also "maxval", "minval", "product", "sum" can have a 3rd optional mask argument.
3375  bool isArrayReductionFunction =
3376  matchingName(s,"all") || matchingName(s,"any") || matchingName(s,"count") || matchingName(s,"maxval") || matchingName(s,"minval") || matchingName(s,"product") || matchingName(s,"sum");
3377 
3378  bool isArrayInqueryFunction =
3379  matchingName(s,"allocated") || matchingName(s,"lbound") || matchingName(s,"shape") || matchingName(s,"size") || matchingName(s,"ubound");
3380 
3381  bool isArrayConstructionAndManipulationFunction =
3382  matchingName(s,"merge") || matchingName(s,"pack") || matchingName(s,"unpack") || matchingName(s,"reshape") || matchingName(s,"spread") || matchingName(s,"cshift") || matchingName(s,"eoshift") || matchingName(s,"transpose");
3383 
3384  // These come in two flavors (depending of the use of s "dim" 2nd argument)
3385  bool isTransformationFunctionForGeometricLocation =
3386  matchingName(s,"maxloc") || matchingName(s,"minloc") || matchingName(s,"unpack") || matchingName(s,"reshape") || matchingName(s,"spread") || matchingName(s,"cshift") || matchingName(s,"eoshift") || matchingName(s,"transpose");
3387 
3388  bool isTransformationFunctionForPointerDisassociation = matchingName(s,"null");
3389 
3390  // These are procedures and so are part of a call statement.
3391  bool isTimeFunction = matchingName(s,"data_and_time") || matchingName(s,"system_clock") || matchingName(s,"cpu_time");
3392 
3393  // These are procedures and so are part of a call statement.
3394  bool isSupportForRandomNumberFunction = matchingName(s,"random_number") || matchingName(s,"random_seed");
3395 
3396  // DQ (11/25/2007): New Fortran 2003 intrinsic functions
3397  bool isNewFortran2003Function = matchingName(s,"is_iostat_end") || matchingName(s,"is_iostat_eor") || matchingName(s,"new_line");
3398 
3399  // These are the generic intrinsic function name tests.
3400  if ( isTypeInqueryFunction || isElementalNumericFunction || isElementalNonConversionFunction ||
3401  isElementalMathFunction || isCharacterConversionFunction || isLexicalCompareFunction ||
3402  isStringHandlingElementalFunction || isLogicalConversionFunction || isStringInqueryFunction ||
3403  isStringTransformationFunction || isNumericInqueryFunction || isElementalRealFunction ||
3404  isKindTransformationFunction || isBitInqueryFunction || isBitElementalFunction ||
3405  isBitElementalSubroutine || isTransferFunction || isVectorMatrixMultipyFunction ||
3406  isArrayReductionFunction || isArrayInqueryFunction || isArrayConstructionAndManipulationFunction ||
3407  isTransformationFunctionForGeometricLocation || isTransformationFunctionForPointerDisassociation ||
3408  isTimeFunction || isSupportForRandomNumberFunction || isNewFortran2003Function)
3409  {
3410  resultValue = true;
3411  }

3808 SgType*
3809 generateIntrinsicFunctionReturnType( string s , SgExprListExp* argumentList )

3826  {

3828

3849 
3850  // Use the implicit type rules, however that is not likely good enough since

3858 SgType*
3859 generateImplicitType( string name )

3861  // Implement the default implicit type rules.
3862  // These will have to be modified to account for user defined implicit type rules later.
3863 
3864  // The DEFAULT implicit typing is based on the first letter of the name Implicit type
3865  // A to H REAL
3866  // I to N INTEGER
3867  // O to Z REAL

3869  SgType* returnType = NULL;
3870 
3871 #if 0
3872  // Output debugging information about saved state (stack) information.
3873  outputState("At TOP of generateImplicitType()");
3874 #endif

3876  // DQ (12/29/2010): Need to search for implicit statement in outer scope (if it exists)

3879  // details correct. This is out outstanding bug in ROSE and show up
3880  // in the latest work reimplementing the R612 and R613 rules.

3882  ROSE_ASSERT(tolower(name[0]) >= 'a');

3884 
3885  // printf ("***** In generateImplicitType(): name = %s name[0] = %c tolower(name[0]) = %c \n",name.c_str(),name[0],tolower(name[0]));
3886

3891  else
3892  {
3893  if (tolower(name[0]) < 'o')
3894  {
3895  returnType = SgTypeInt::createType();
3896  }
3897  else
3898  {
3899  returnType = SgTypeFloat::createType();
3900  }
3901  }
3902 
3903  // printf ("***** name = %s generating type = %s \n",name.c_str(),returnType->class_name().c_str());
3904

3910 
3911 SgFunctionType* generateImplicitFunctionType( string functionName)
3912  {
3913  // This function generates a function type that is computed from the name of the function
3914  // and the types of the function arguments on the stack (astExpressionStack).
3915 
3916  bool isIntrinsicFunction = matchAgainstIntrinsicFunctionList(functionName);
3917  bool argumentListOnStack = ( (astExpressionStack.empty() == false) && (isSgExprListExp(astExpressionStack.front()) != NULL) );
3918 
3919  SgType* returnType = NULL;
3920  SgExprListExp* exprListExp = NULL;
3921 
3922  // printf ("argumentListOnStack = %s \n",argumentListOnStack ? "true" : "false");
3923  // printf ("isIntrinsicFunction = %s \n",isIntrinsicFunction ? "true" : "false");
3924  if (argumentListOnStack == true)
3925  {
3926  // If there is an argument list, then if it is a non-empty list then the return type of
3927  // the function is determined by the argument type.
3928  exprListExp = isSgExprListExp(astExpressionStack.front());
3929 
3930  if (isIntrinsicFunction == true)
3931  {
3932  returnType = generateIntrinsicFunctionReturnType(functionName,exprListExp);
3933  }
3934  else
3935  {
3936  // We need to lookup the type by looking for a variable in the symbol table and using that type
3937  returnType = generateImplicitType(functionName);
3938  }
3939  }
3940  else
3941  {
3942  // This may be just a request to generate a function type from a function name.
3943  // In this case the type can not yet be precisely defined so we use some defaults
3944  // for the parts that we don't know (and fixup the information later in post-processing
3945  // phases).
3946  if (isIntrinsicFunction == true)
3947  {
3948  returnType = generateIntrinsicFunctionReturnType(functionName,NULL);
3949  }
3950  else
3951  {
3952  // We need to lookup the type by looking for a variable in the symbol table and using that type
3953  returnType = generateImplicitType(functionName);
3954  }
3955 
3956  }
3957 
3958  bool has_ellipses = false;
3959  SgFunctionType* functionType = new SgFunctionType(returnType,has_ellipses);
3960  ROSE_ASSERT(functionType != NULL);
3961  ROSE_ASSERT(functionType->get_argument_list() != NULL);
3962 #if 0
3963  printf ("######################################### functionType = %p ####################################### \n",functionType);
3964 #endif
3965 
3966  if (argumentListOnStack == true)
3967  {
3968  // If there was a SgExprListExp on the stack, then fillin the SgFunctionType with the types of the arguments.
3969  ROSE_ASSERT(exprListExp != NULL);
3970  SgExpressionPtrList & functionArgumentList = exprListExp->get_expressions();
3971  for (unsigned int i=0; i < functionArgumentList.size(); i++)
3972  {
3973  functionType->append_argument(functionArgumentList[i]->get_type());
3974  }
3975  }
3976 
3977  return functionType;
3978  }

4264  // These represent special Fortran specific support in ROSE.

4290  default:

4300  case AttrSpec_INTRINSIC: variableDeclaration->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().setIntrinsic(); break;

4305  case AttrSpec_COTARGET: break; // DXN (04/11/2011): TODO
4306  case AttrSpec_VALUE: variableDeclaration->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().setValue(); break;

4462 void
4463 convertExpressionOnStackToFunctionCallExp()
4464  {

4466 
4467  // This function takes a varRefExp on the astExpressionStack and converts it to a function call of the same name.
4468  // This addresses to need to be able to change the type of construct represented initially with little information
4469  // and so for which we assumed it was a variable and only later in the sequence of parsing actions discovered that
4470  // it was a function. In general everything is a function unless there is a hint that it is an array.

4472 #if 0

4495  {
4496  // DQ (1/20/2008): Added support to fix test2007_164.f (calling functions without the "()" syntax)
4497  SgFunctionRefExp* functionRefExp = isSgFunctionRefExp(expression);

4500  SgExprListExp* functionArguments = new SgExprListExp();

4502

4508 
4509  // Now push the function call to the implicit function onto the astExpressionStack
4510  ROSE_ASSERT(functionCallExp != NULL);
4511  astExpressionStack.push_front(functionCallExp);
4512  }
4513  else
4514  {
4515  // printf ("In convertExpressionOnStackToFunctionCallExp(): expression = %p = %s \n",expression,expression->class_name().c_str());

4669 SgFunctionRefExp*
4670 generateFunctionRefExp( Token_t* nameToken )
4671  {
4672  // This function will generate a SgFunctionRefExp using just the function name and the current scope.
4673  // If the function is found in a symbol table (iterating from the current scope to the global scope)
4674  // then the SgFunctionRefExp is built using the found SgFunctionSymbol.
4675  // If no SgFunctionSymbol is found in the symbol tables from iterating through all the scopes, then
4676  // a new SgProcedureHeaderStatement (function declaration) is built and an associated SgFunctionSymbol
4677  // is inserted into the global scope.
4678 
4679  // Note that the global scope may not be correct if the function will be seen later in
4680  // a different scope (e.g. the current module's scope). So a fixup is required and is
4681  // called from R1106 c_action_end_module_stmt().
4682 
4683  ROSE_ASSERT(nameToken != NULL);
4684  std::string name = nameToken->text;
4685 
4686  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
4687  printf ("Generating a SgFunctionRefExp for name = %s \n",name.c_str());
4688 
4689  SgFunctionType* functionType = generateImplicitFunctionType(name);
4690  ROSE_ASSERT(functionType != NULL);
4691 
4692  // The next element on the stack is the expression list of function arguments
4693  // ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.empty() == false);
4694  // SgExprListExp* functionArguments = isSgExprListExp(astExpressionStack.front());
4695  // astExpressionStack.pop_front();
4696 
4697  SgFunctionRefExp* functionRefExp = NULL;
4698  SgName functionName = nameToken->text;
4699  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol(functionName,astScopeStack.front());
4700 
4701 #if 0
4702  printf ("In generateFunctionRefExp(): called trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol() -- functionSymbol = %p \n",functionSymbol);
4703 #endif
4704 
4705  if (functionSymbol != NULL)
4706  {
4707  // Found the function symbol, so build the function ref expression using the existing symbol...
4708  // printf ("Found the function symbol, so build the function ref expression using the existing symbol... \n");
4709 
4710  functionRefExp = new SgFunctionRefExp(functionSymbol,NULL);
4711  setSourcePosition(functionRefExp);
4712  }
4713  else
4714  {
4715  // If the function has not been seen yet, it does not mean that it is an array. It could be a function
4716  // to be declared later or an intrinsic function. But the point is that it is a function!
4717 
4718  // For implicit function we build non-defining declarations
4719  SgFunctionDefinition* functionDefinition = NULL;
4720  // SgFunctionDeclaration* functionDeclaration = new SgFunctionDeclaration(name,functionType,functionDefinition);
4721  // SgProgramHeaderStatement* functionDeclaration = new SgProgramHeaderStatement(name,functionType,functionDefinition);
4722  SgProcedureHeaderStatement* functionDeclaration = new SgProcedureHeaderStatement(name,functionType,functionDefinition);
4723 
4724  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
4725  printf ("Generated a SgProcedureHeaderStatement for name = %s functionDeclaration = %p \n",name.c_str(),functionDeclaration);
4726 
4727  // This is the first function declaration for this function name so we have to set it as the firstNondefiningDeclaration.
4728  // Note that the first nondefining declaration is what is always used for building symbols.
4729  functionDeclaration->set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(functionDeclaration);
4730  functionDeclaration->set_definingDeclaration(NULL);
4731 
4732  // Set the parent to the global scope, mostly just to have it be non-NULL (checked by internal error checking).
4733  ROSE_ASSERT(astScopeStack.empty() == false);
4734 
4735  // We really want the nearest module scope or global scope is there is no module scope.
4736  // See test2010_140.f90
4737  // SgScopeStatement* currentScope = astScopeStack.front();
4738  SgScopeStatement* currentScope = isSgClassDefinition(astScopeStack.front());
4739  if (currentScope == NULL)
4740  {
4741  currentScope = TransformationSupport::getClassDefinition(astScopeStack.front());
4742  if (currentScope == NULL)
4743  {
4744  currentScope = TransformationSupport::getGlobalScope(astScopeStack.front());
4745  ROSE_ASSERT(currentScope != NULL);
4746  }
4747  }
4748  ROSE_ASSERT(currentScope != NULL);
4749 
4750  functionDeclaration->set_parent(currentScope);
4751  functionDeclaration->set_scope(currentScope);
4752  functionDeclaration->set_subprogram_kind(SgProcedureHeaderStatement::e_function_subprogram_kind);
4753  setSourcePosition(functionDeclaration,nameToken);
4754  // We should not have to set this explicitly!
4755  setSourcePosition(functionDeclaration->get_parameterList(),nameToken);
4756 
4757  // Now build the function call and use the arguments from the ExprList on the top of the astExpressionStack!
4758  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = new SgFunctionSymbol(functionDeclaration);
4759 
4760  // Insert the function into the global scope so that we can find it later
4761  currentScope->insert_symbol(functionName,functionSymbol);
4762 
4763  functionRefExp = new SgFunctionRefExp(functionSymbol,NULL);
4764  setSourcePosition(functionRefExp);
4765  }
4766 
4767  // Now push the function call to the implicit function onto the astExpressionStack
4768  ROSE_ASSERT(functionRefExp != NULL);
4769  // astExpressionStack.push_front(functionRefExp);
4770 
4771  return functionRefExp;
4772  }

4957 buildProcedureSupport(SgProcedureHeaderStatement* procedureDeclaration, bool hasDummyArgList)
4958  {
4959  // This does not do everything required to build a function or subroutine, but it does as much as possible
4960  // (factors out code so that it can be called for R1117, R1224, and R1232.
4961 
4962  // This will be the defining declaration
4963  ROSE_ASSERT(procedureDeclaration != NULL);
4964 
4965  procedureDeclaration->set_definingDeclaration(procedureDeclaration);
4966  procedureDeclaration->set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(NULL);
4967 
4968  ROSE_ASSERT(astScopeStack.empty() == false);
4969  SgScopeStatement* currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration = astScopeStack.front();
4970 
4971  ROSE_ASSERT(currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration != NULL);
4972 
4973  // This should not be a SgFunctionDefinition, but it can be a SgBasicBlock (currently) if it is declared in an Interface.
4974  // ROSE_ASSERT(isSgBasicBlock(currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration) == NULL);
4975  ROSE_ASSERT(isSgFunctionDefinition(currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration) == NULL);
4976 
4977  if (astInterfaceStack.empty() == false)
4978  {
4979  SgInterfaceStatement* interfaceStatement = astInterfaceStack.front();
4980 
4981  // DQ (10/6/2008): The use of the SgInterfaceBody IR nodes allows the details of if
4982  // it was a procedure name or a procedure declaration to be abstracted away and saves
4983  // this detail of how it was structured in the source code in the AST (for the unparser).
4984  SgName name = procedureDeclaration->get_name();

4986  // the SgInterfaceBody. Check if interfaceStatement and the procedureDeclaration are in

4989  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL)
4990  {
4991  printf("interfacestmt %p scope: %p\n",interfaceStatement, interfaceStmtScope);
4992  printf("procedure %p scope: %p\n",procedureDeclaration, currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration);
4993  }
4994  if (interfaceStmtScope == currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration)
4995  {
4996  SgInterfaceBody* interfaceBody = new SgInterfaceBody(name,procedureDeclaration,/*use_function_name*/ false);
4997  procedureDeclaration->set_parent(interfaceStatement);
4998  interfaceStatement->get_interface_body_list().push_back(interfaceBody);
4999  interfaceBody->set_parent(interfaceStatement);
5000  setSourcePosition(interfaceBody);
5001  }
5002  }
5003  else
5004  {
5005  // The function was not processed as part of an interface so add it to the current scope.
5006  currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration->append_statement(procedureDeclaration);
5007  }
5008 
5009  // Go looking for if this was a previously declared function
5010  // SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol(procedureDeclaration->get_name(),astScopeStack.front());
5011  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_function_symbol(procedureDeclaration->get_name(),currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration);
5012 
5013 #if 0

5016  printf ("In buildProcedureSupport(): procedureDeclaration scope = %p \n",procedureDeclaration->get_scope());
5017  printf ("In buildProcedureSupport(): currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration = %p = %s \n",currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration,currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration->class_name().c_str());
5018 #endif
5019 
5020  if (functionSymbol != NULL)
5021  {
5022  SgFunctionDeclaration* nondefiningDeclaration = functionSymbol->get_declaration();
5023  ROSE_ASSERT(nondefiningDeclaration != NULL);
5024 
5025  procedureDeclaration->set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(nondefiningDeclaration);
5026 
5027  // And set the defining declaration in the non-defining declaration
5028  nondefiningDeclaration->set_definingDeclaration(procedureDeclaration);
5029 
5030  // update scope information
5031  if (nondefiningDeclaration->get_scope()->symbol_exists(functionSymbol))
5032  {
5033  nondefiningDeclaration->get_scope()->remove_symbol(functionSymbol);
5034  }
5035  nondefiningDeclaration->set_scope(currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration);
5036  nondefiningDeclaration->set_parent(currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration);
5037  currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration->insert_symbol(nondefiningDeclaration->get_name(), functionSymbol);
5038  functionSymbol->set_declaration(procedureDeclaration); // update the defining declaration
5039  }
5040  else
5041  {

5045  currentScopeOfFunctionDeclaration->insert_symbol(procedureDeclaration->get_name(), functionSymbol);

5140  ROSE_ASSERT(astNameStack.empty() == false);

5415  ROSE_ASSERT(subscript != NULL);
5416 
5417  // This could be a integer expression or a SgSubscriptExpression
5418  SgSubscriptExpression* subscriptExpression = isSgSubscriptExpression(subscript);
5419  if (subscriptExpression != NULL)
5420  {
5421  // Set the parents of all the parts of the SgSubscriptExpression
5422  subscriptExpression->get_lowerBound()->set_parent(subscript);
5423  subscriptExpression->get_upperBound()->set_parent(subscript);
5424  subscriptExpression->get_stride()->set_parent(subscript);
5425 
5426  // Only set the position of the new SgSubscriptExpression, not a previously built integer expression.
5427  setSourcePosition(subscriptExpression);
5428  }
5429 
5430  ROSE_ASSERT(subscript != NULL);
5431  return subscript;
5432  }

5437 isPubliclyAccessible( SgSymbol* symbol )
5438  {
5439  bool returnValue = false;
5440  SgNode* symbol_basis = symbol->get_symbol_basis();
5441 
5442  SgDeclarationStatement* declaration = isSgDeclarationStatement(symbol_basis);
5443  if (declaration != NULL)
5444  {
5445  // printf ("In isPubliclyAccessible(): declaration = %p = %s symbol = %s \n",declaration,declaration->class_name().c_str(),symbol->get_name().str());
5446 
5447  // Publically accessible is either declared explicitly as public, or not defined as anything (default in Fortran is public).
5448 #if 1
5449  // DQ (8/16/2020): We changed the definition of isDefault to not be equivalent to isPublic (required for C++ handling).
5450  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isPublic() == true ||
5451  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isDefault() == true ||
5452  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isUndefined() == true)
5453 #else
5454  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isPublic() == true ||
5455  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isUndefined() == true)
5456 #endif
5457  {
5458  returnValue = true;
5459  }
5460 
5461  // declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().display("In isPubliclyAccessible()");
5462  }
5463  else
5464  {
5465  SgInitializedName* initializedName = isSgInitializedName(symbol_basis);
5466  if (initializedName != NULL)
5467  {
5468  SgNode* parent = initializedName->get_parent();
5469  SgDeclarationStatement* declaration = isSgDeclarationStatement(parent);
5470  if (declaration != NULL)
5471  {
5472 #if 0
5473  // printf ("declaration (from SgInitializedName) = %p = %s \n",declaration,declaration->class_name().c_str());
5474  printf ("In isPubliclyAccessible(): declaration = %p = %s symbol = %s \n",declaration,declaration->class_name().c_str(),symbol->get_name().str());
5475  declaration->get_declarationModifier().display("In isPubliclyAccessible()");
5476 #endif
5477 #if 1
5478  // DQ (8/16/2020): We changed the definition of isDefault to not be equivalent to isPublic (required for C++ handling).
5479  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isPublic() == true ||
5480  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isDefault() == true ||
5481  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isUndefined() == true)
5482 #else
5483  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isPublic() == true ||
5484  declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().isUndefined() == true)
5485 #endif
5486  {
5487  returnValue = true;
5488  }
5489  else
5490  {
5491  // DQ (9/11/2010): See test2007_176.f03 for an example of the F2003 use of the "protected" keyword.
5492  // If it was marked as protected in the variable then either it will be found in a parent scope
5493  // (for module functions) or it should not be put into the current scope as an aliased variable symbol.
5494  // printf ("This may still be a protected variable. \n");
5495 
5496  // DQ (9/11/2010): But make sure this is not marked as protected (is so then we want to include it as an aliased symbol).
5497  if (initializedName->get_protected_declaration() == true)
5498  {
5499  // This should not be considered a publicly accessible variable (don't put it into the synbol table as an aliased symbol.
5500  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
5501  printf ("In isPubliclyAccessible(): Note that this variable is marked as protected (so must be included as an aliased symbol \n");
5502 
5503  returnValue = true;
5504  }
5505  }
5506 
5507  // declaration->get_declarationModifier().get_accessModifier().display("In isPubliclyAccessible()");
5508  }
5509  }
5510  else
5511  {
5512  // This case is not handled yet
5513  printf ("In isPubliclyAccessible(): Uknown symbol_basis = %p = %s \n",symbol_basis,symbol_basis->class_name().c_str());
5514  ROSE_ABORT();
5515  }

5518  // Pei-Hung (07/26/2019) Check if access attribute is given in SgAttributeSpecificationStatement
5519  // Test case avaiable in test2019_private_attribute.f90 & test2019_private_attribute2.f90
5520  SgScopeStatement* scope = symbol->get_scope();
5521  SgFunctionDefinition* functionDefinition = isSgFunctionDefinition(scope);
5522  if (functionDefinition != NULL)
5523  {
5524  std::vector<SgStatement*>::iterator j = functionDefinition->get_body()->get_statements().begin();
5525  while ( j != functionDefinition->get_body()->get_statements().end() )
5526  {
5527  // Look for the access attribute in SgAttributeSpecificationStatement
5528  SgAttributeSpecificationStatement* attributeStmt = isSgAttributeSpecificationStatement(*j);
5529  if (attributeStmt != NULL)
5530  {
5531  SgStringList& nameList = attributeStmt->get_name_list();
5532  SgStringList::iterator i = nameList.begin();
5533  while(i != nameList.end())
5534  {
5535  if((*i).compare(symbol->get_name().str()) == 0)
5536  {
5537  if(attributeStmt->get_attribute_kind() == SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::e_accessStatement_private)
5538  returnValue = false;
5539  else if(attributeStmt->get_attribute_kind() == SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::e_accessStatement_public)
5540  returnValue = true;
5541  }
5542  i++;
5543  }
5544  }
5545  j++;
5546  }
5547  }
5548  // Pei-Hung (07/25/2019) search for implicit statement in modules
5549  SgClassDefinition* classDefinition = isSgClassDefinition(scope);
5550  if (classDefinition != NULL)
5551  {
5552  SgDeclarationStatementPtrList& declStmtList = classDefinition->get_members();
5553  SgDeclarationStatementPtrList::const_iterator j = declStmtList.begin();
5554  while (j != declStmtList.end())
5555  {
5556  // Look for the access attribute in SgAttributeSpecificationStatement
5557  SgAttributeSpecificationStatement* attributeStmt = isSgAttributeSpecificationStatement(*j);
5558  if (attributeStmt != NULL)
5559  {
5560  SgStringList& nameList = attributeStmt->get_name_list();
5561  SgStringList::iterator i = nameList.begin();
5562  while(i != nameList.end())
5563  {
5564  if((*i).compare(symbol->get_name().str()) == 0)
5565  {
5566  if(attributeStmt->get_attribute_kind() == SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::e_accessStatement_private)
5567  returnValue = false;
5568  else if(attributeStmt->get_attribute_kind() == SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::e_accessStatement_public)
5569  returnValue = true;
5570  }
5571  i++;
5572  }
5573  }
5574  j++;
5575  }
5576  }
5577 
5578 
5579  return returnValue;
5580  }

5582 void
5583 cleanupTypeStackAfterDeclaration()
5584  {
5585  // This function is called in R501 c_action_type_declaration_stmt().
5586 
5587  // We should have used all the types stored on the stack at this point!
5588  // Except for the case of an array type which will have pushed the base type
5589  // onto the stack and then an array type. In this case we will still have
5590  // the base type on the stack. If there was a scalar variable then it will
5591  // have used the type on the stack, but we should take care of this by always
5592  // pushing a type onto the stack for each variable to use and then making
5593  // sure that we have the base type still on the stack at this point, so the
5594  // stack at this point should never be empty and should have the unused base
5595  // type on top (and the stack size should be 1).
5596 
5597  if (astTypeStack.empty() == false)
5598  {
5599  // This should be only a base type that has been left on the stack.
5600  // printf ("WARNING, astTypeStack not empty: astTypeStack.front() = %p = %s \n",astTypeStack.front(),astTypeStack.front()->class_name().c_str());
5601 
5602  // If there was an array declaration then the base type is left on the stack, else
5603  // the stack is empty. Cleanup the stack of the one possible base type left there!
5604  // astTypeStack.pop_front();
5605 
5606  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
5607  printf ("WARNING, astTypeStack not empty: astTypeStack.front() = %p = %s = %s (CLEARING astTypeStack) \n",astTypeStack.front(),astTypeStack.front()->class_name().c_str(),SageInterface::get_name(astTypeStack.front()).c_str());
5608 
5609  astTypeStack.clear();
5610 #if 0
5611  if (astTypeStack.empty() == false)
5612  outputState("Error: astTypeStack.empty() == false in R502 c_action_declaration_type_spec()");
5613 #endif
5614  ROSE_ASSERT(astTypeStack.empty() == true);
5615  }
5616 
5617  if (astBaseTypeStack.empty() == false)
5618  {
5619  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
5620  printf ("WARNING, astBaseTypeStack not empty: astBaseTypeStack.front() = %p = %s = %s (CLEARING astBaseTypeStack) \n",astBaseTypeStack.front(),astBaseTypeStack.front()->class_name().c_str(),SageInterface::get_name(astBaseTypeStack.front()).c_str());
5621 
5622  astBaseTypeStack.clear();
5623 #if 0
5624  if (astBaseTypeStack.empty() == false)
5625  outputState("Error: astBaseTypeStack.empty() == false in R502 c_action_declaration_type_spec()");
5626 #endif
5627  ROSE_ASSERT(astBaseTypeStack.empty() == true);
5628  }
5629  }
