5708 void
5709 generateAssignmentStatement(Token_t* label, bool isPointerAssignment )
5710  {
5711  // This function builds the SgAssignOp and the SgExprStatement and
5712  // inserts it into the current scope.
5713 
5714 #if 0
5715  // Output debugging information about saved state (stack) information.
5716  outputState("At TOP of generateAssignmentStatement()");
5717 #endif
5718 
5719  ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.empty() == false);
5720  SgExpression* rhs = astExpressionStack.front();
5721  astExpressionStack.pop_front();
5722 
5723  ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.empty() == false);
5724  SgExpression* lhs = astExpressionStack.front();
5725  astExpressionStack.pop_front();
5726 
5727  // Note that the type provided is NULL, since ROSE will internally (dynamically) evaluate the type
5728  // as required. This avoids state in the AST and better supports transformations on the AST.
5729  // SgAssignOp* assignmentExpr = new SgAssignOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
5730  SgExpression* assignmentExpr = NULL;
5731  if (isPointerAssignment == true)
5732  {
5733  // This is "p => x"
5734  assignmentExpr = new SgPointerAssignOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
5735  }
5736  else
5737  {
5738  // This is "p = x"
5739  assignmentExpr = new SgAssignOp(lhs,rhs,NULL);
5740  }
5741 
5742  setSourcePosition(assignmentExpr);
5743 
5744  // DQ (1/22/2008): Set the source position based on the internal expressions
5745  resetSourcePosition(assignmentExpr,lhs);
5746  // resetSourcePosition(assignmentExpr,rhs);
5747 
5748  // Now build the expression statement required for insertion into the current
5749  // scope (note that expressions cannot be directly inserted into scopes).
5750 
5751  SgExprStatement* expressionStatement = new SgExprStatement(assignmentExpr);
5752 
5753  if (label != NULL)
5754  {
5755  // A label was provided so set the label in the expressionStatement
5756 
5757  // Setup the label on the statement if it is available.
5758  setStatementNumericLabel(expressionStatement,label);
5759 
5760  // If there is a label then at least try to use it to set the source
5761  // position approximately (better than nothing).
5762  setSourcePosition(expressionStatement,label);
5763  }
5764  else
5765  {
5766  // No source position information is available
5767  setSourcePosition(expressionStatement);
5768 
5769  // DQ (1/22/2008): Try this
5770  resetSourcePosition(expressionStatement,assignmentExpr);
5771  }
5772 
5773  setStatementNumericLabelUsingStack(expressionStatement);
5774 
5775  // DQ (1/31/2009): Moved this to the TOP of the function.
5776  // Refactored the code to build support function
5777  // initialize_global_scope_if_required();
5778  // build_implicit_program_statement_if_required();
5779 
5780  SgScopeStatement* currentScope = getTopOfScopeStack();
5781  currentScope->append_statement(expressionStatement);
5782 
5783  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL )
5784  printf ("Pushing this expressionStatement onto the astNodeStack for optional use by where statement \n");
5785 
5786  // This is needed for test2007_67.f90
5787  astNodeStack.push_front(expressionStatement);
5788 
5789 #if 0
5790  // Output debugging information about saved state (stack) information.
5791  outputState("At BOTTOM of generateAssignmentStatement()");
5792 #endif
5793 
5794  // Error checking for astExpressionStack
5795  ROSE_ASSERT(astScopeStack.empty() == false);
5796  ROSE_ASSERT(astScopeStack.front()->get_parent() != NULL);
5797  SgWhereStatement* whereStatement = isSgWhereStatement(astScopeStack.front()->get_parent());
5798  SgIfStmt* ifStatement = isSgIfStmt(astScopeStack.front()->get_parent());
5799  if (whereStatement != NULL || ifStatement != NULL)
5800  {
5801  // If in a where statement produced with R 619:section-subscript-list__begin then the
5802  // condition is on the stack, else if it was produced with R744:where-construct-stmt
5803  // then the condition was used directly and already cleared from the stack.
5804  // ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.empty() == false);
5805  ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.size() <= 1);
5806  }
5807  else
5808  {
5809  // If this is NOT a where statement then the stack should be empty.
5810  ROSE_ASSERT(astExpressionStack.empty() == true);
5811  }
5812  }

5883 void
5884 fixupModuleScope( SgClassDefinition* moduleScope )
5885  {
5886  // Fixes up function symbols to be in the correct scope when the function call appears before the function declaration.
5887  ROSE_ASSERT(moduleScope != NULL);
5888 
5889  ROSE_ASSERT(moduleScope->containsOnlyDeclarations() == true);
5890  const SgDeclarationStatementPtrList & declarationList = moduleScope->getDeclarationList();
5891 
5892  // printf ("Inside of fixupModuleScope(moduleScope = %p) \n",moduleScope);
5893 
5894  SgDeclarationStatementPtrList::const_iterator i = declarationList.begin();
5895  while (i != declarationList.end())
5896  {
5897  SgProcedureHeaderStatement* functionDeclaration = isSgProcedureHeaderStatement(*i);
5898  if (functionDeclaration != NULL)
5899  {
5900  // Note that at this point where fixupModuleScope() is called the astScopeStack has already poped the module scope.
5901  // So a valid local_symbol means that the declaration was not placed into the module scope (e.g incorrectly placed
5902  // into the global scope).
5903 
5904  // Test if there is a valid symbol associated with each function declaration.
5905  SgSymbol* tempSymbol = functionDeclaration->get_symbol_from_symbol_table();
5906  if (tempSymbol == NULL)
5907  {
5908  // These function without a valid symbol need to be fixed up.
5909  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 0 )
5910  printf ("(tempSymbol == NULL): Identified a function declaration = %p = %s = %s \n",functionDeclaration,functionDeclaration->class_name().c_str(),functionDeclaration->get_name().str());
5911 
5912  SgName variableName = functionDeclaration->get_name();
5913  SgVariableSymbol* variableSymbol = NULL;
5914  SgFunctionSymbol* functionSymbol = NULL;
5915  SgClassSymbol* classSymbol = NULL;
5916 
5917  trace_back_through_parent_scopes_lookup_variable_symbol_but_do_not_build_variable(variableName,moduleScope,variableSymbol,functionSymbol,classSymbol);
5918 
5919  if (functionSymbol != NULL)
5920  {
5921  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL )
5922  printf ("Found functionSymbol = %p function name = %s (erasing all traces of this function in the wrong scope) \n",functionSymbol,variableName.str());
5923 
5924  SgSymbolTable* symbolTable = isSgSymbolTable(functionSymbol->get_parent());
5925  ROSE_ASSERT(symbolTable != NULL);
5926 
5927  // Remove the symbol from the scope were it was first put (incorrectly).
5928  symbolTable->remove(functionSymbol);
5929 
5930  // Insert the functionSymbol into the moduleScope
5931  moduleScope->insert_symbol(variableName,functionSymbol);
5932  }
5933  else
5934  {
5935  // DQ (8/28/2010): Report more diagnostics.
5936  printf ("Warning: In fixupModuleScope() there was no SgFunctionSymbol found reset into the module scope \n");
5937  }
5938  }
5939  else
5940  {
5941  // These functions don't require any fixup.
5942  // printf ("(local_symbol != NULL): Identified a function declaration = %p = %s = %s \n",functionDeclaration,functionDeclaration->class_name().c_str(),functionDeclaration->get_name().str());
5943  }
5944  }
5945 
5946  i++;
5947  }
5948  }

6332

6339 
6340  // If the array spec is a part of the multi-part reference then process it as such and build the type on the astTypeStack (specific for that variable), else build it for the astBaseTypeStack for all variables.
6341  // if (hasArraySpec == true)
6342  // printf ("In processAttributeSpecStack(): hasArraySpec = %s hasInitialization = %s \n",hasArraySpec ? "true" : "false", hasInitialization ? "true" : "false");
6343 
6344  // DQ (1/22/2011): Not clear now to handle hasInitialization...

6346  // if (hasArraySpec == true)

6348 
6349  if (hasInitialization == false)
6350  {
6351  if ((astTypeStack.empty() == true) || (hasArraySpec == true) ) // This is a problem for test2011_16.f90

6353  if (hasArraySpec == true)

6356  int count = 1;
